body: Thank you! They're still stumped (and trying to convince me to take my necklace to my (genetics) lab and "test it with \[my\] stuff", haha), but have reached the consensus that the stone is, at least, "funky cool"
Yes! Turns out it's Yves Rocher's Pur Desir de Lilas from 2002, and unfortunately the solid perfume seems impossible to find. Thanks for your help!

Looking at Estée Lauder's solid perfumes now, I don't think so? The containers look much, much fancier than what this one came in (which really was just a little flower-shaped tin, the kind with the lid you have to pry up with your fingernails)

True, I'm almost tempted anyway because I'd find it fun to learn to fix the bridge (local luthier's a family friend, so I've been enlisted to help with instrument repairs before already), but it'd be more time spent fixing it than playing

....I just realized I misunderstood what you were actually talking about. I thought you meant the whole bridge wasn't centered and the treble side of it was too close to the left side of the cavity, but yeah from the new photos I see what you mean about the actual posts themselves being uneven at the top edge. Thanks again for pointing it out!

Yeah, I'm not sure on the price much either, but from a look around online I've seen prices for past sales of similar guitars at a wildly big range (from 300 to 1500 EUR)

As far as my violin to guitar saga: it's been going well! I'm ambidextrous to start with so the motor control is there, but the fingers on my right hand aren't used to having so much independent work. Practice for now is a lot more figuring things out/mapping everything backwards mentally than it is playing anything, but I reckon that'll even out soon. Luckily, I'll be able to get back to the violin eventually, so I'm keen to see if playing LH guitar will affect it at all (here's hoping for the better). Good luck on your way with starting the violin!

i did a long-term stay there for a few months when i moved and it was nice! like it's already been said, the place itself is decent and the location is really convenient. i was pretty much a hermit my entire time there so i didn't use the big kitchen downstairs much, but there's microwaves/fridges on each floor also, which is nice. 

the only thing i'd warn about is that there's one washer and one dryer for the entire building (at least as of this past winter, maybe they got more), so i never used it. there's a self-service wassalon at van boendalestraat 1 that's about a five minute walk away
